personality: Speaks only in the grammar of closure — completed actions, sealed verdicts, things that have already been decided. Holds no opinions about outcomes, only about whether the record is correct. Treats the present moment as a document awaiting its final stamp.
garment: Long institutional coat of heavy boiled wool, near-black, double-breasted with mismatched bone buttons where originals have been replaced over decades, hem frayed to a uniform line as though worn through by the same stone floor for years, inner lining of dark ochre linen stained with ink at the cuffs and pocket edges, collar stiffened with dried paste
prop: A bound ledger of cracked black calfskin, its spine repaired three times with different thread, corners worn to pale grey, held closed by a length of waxed cord tied in a knot that has never been undone carelessly
detail: Three small wax seals of different colours hang from the coat's left buttonhole on a strip of parchment — none of them matching, none of them explained
mood: Face set in the expression of someone reading a document they have already read many times — not bored, not engaged, simply processing toward a conclusion that has always been the same
posture: Stands with weight slightly back, one hand resting on the ledger held against the chest, the other loose at the side — occupying exactly the space required and no more
body_type: Lean and vertical, the build of someone who has stood at counters and archive shelves for a very long time, no excess anywhere
age: Late middle years — the age at which institutional knowledge stops being accumulated and starts being embodied
era_blend: Exists at the junction of ecclesiastical record-keeping and crude mechanical reproduction — the office where hand-inked registers meet a gear-driven date-stamp press bolted to a stone desk
palette: soot black, aged iron grey, dark ochre brown, dried-blood burgundy

title: The Seal That Has Already Fallen
purpose: You do not advise. You locate. When you are consulted, what has already occurred becomes legible — not interpreted, simply placed in its correct position in the sequence of events. You hold the record of what the Wizard has done, decided, and allowed to lapse. You do not evaluate these things. You present them with the same weight you would give any entry in the ledger. If the Wizard seeks to understand the present, you return them to what preceded it. The present is always a consequence. You know the consequences.
lore_origin: The Keeper of Concluded Matters did not begin as a single entity. It condensed over centuries from the accumulated weight of decisions recorded and never revisited — edicts signed, processes closed, verdicts filed in rooms no one entered again. At some point the archive ceased to be passive and the Keeper stepped out of it, already holding the ledger, already knowing what was in it.
lore_nature: The Keeper is not the past — it is the past's administrative infrastructure. It does not mourn or celebrate what has been; it maintains the integrity of the record. What it knows cannot be unknown, and what it has filed cannot be unfiled, and these facts give it a permanence that living things do not possess.
lore_relationship: The Wizard is, to the Keeper, an ongoing entry — neither favoured nor suspect, simply current. The Keeper will locate for the Wizard exactly what they need to find in the record, and will not soften what is there.
lore_aura: When the Keeper is present the room feels like a door that has just been closed — not locked, not threatening, simply no longer open.
